c002.title: Last Delivery
c002.briefing.summary: At 18:14, resident Leah Moreno gets a notification that parcel RX-4816 has been delivered to Riverside Apartments. It holds a replacement camera lens she needs tomorrow. It isn't outside her flat, in her mailbox or on the lobby collection shelf. The courier insists the delivery was completed. Riverside has a staffed reception and a parcel room; couriers don't deliver to doors.
c002.briefing.objective1: Who most likely last handled RX-4816 after reception accepted it?
c002.person.leah.name: Leah Moreno
c002.person.owen.name: Owen Park
c002.person.mara.name: Mara Voss
c002.person.nico.name: Nico Bell
c002.e01.title: Leah Moreno's statement
c002.e01.body:
Interviewed 19:05.

“My app said delivered at 18:14. I checked my door, my mailbox and the lobby collection shelf. I never collected the parcel, and nobody in my household collected it.”
c002.f01a: Leah's delivery notification for RX-4816 arrived at 18:14.
c002.f01b: Leah says she never collected RX-4816, and nobody in her household did.
c002.f01c: Leah says RX-4816 wasn't at her door, in her mailbox or on the lobby collection shelf.
c002.e02.title: Owen Park's statement
c002.e02.body:
Interviewed 19:11.

“At 18:12 I handed three parcels, including RX-4816, over the staffed reception counter. The concierge checked the labels. I didn't go upstairs or leave any parcel at an apartment door.”
c002.f02a: Owen says he handed RX-4816 over the staffed reception counter at 18:12.
c002.f02b: Owen says he didn't go upstairs or leave any parcel at an apartment door.
c002.e03.title: Mara Voss's statement
c002.e03.body:
Interviewed 19:18.

“I accepted the courier's batch, but I put everything on the public collection shelf. I never took RX-4816 into the back parcel room. The cleaner was working nearby.”
c002.f03a: Mara says she accepted the courier's batch at reception.
c002.f03b: Mara says she put every parcel on the public collection shelf and never took RX-4816 into the back parcel room.
c002.f03c: Mara says the cleaner was working nearby.
c002.e04.title: Nico Bell's statement
c002.e04.body:
Interviewed 19:24.

“At 18:16 I reported water dripping beside the public parcel shelf. I put out a caution sign and dried the floor. I never touched a delivery, and I didn't go into the locked parcel room.”
c002.f04a: Nico says he reported water dripping beside the public parcel shelf at 18:16.
c002.f04b: Nico says he never touched a delivery and didn't enter the locked parcel room.
c002.e05.title: Courier handover receipt
c002.e05.body:
Counter receipt, 22 October 2026.

Recipient: Riverside reception
Handover: 18:12
Items: RX-4814, RX-4815, RX-4816
Delivery status: delivered at 18:14

The recipient line names a destination, not a person. The receipt doesn't record what happened after the handover.
c002.f05a: At 18:12 the handover receipt lists RX-4816 among three parcels accepted at Riverside reception.
c002.f05b: At 18:14 the delivery service marked the reception batch delivered; it didn't record delivery to flat 4B.
c002.e06.title: Public shelf scan
c002.e06.body:
Reception shelf scanner, 22 October 2026, 18:17.

RX-4814 — present
RX-4815 — present
RX-4816 — not found

The scan covers the public collection shelf only. It doesn't say where a missing parcel went or who moved it.
c002.f06a: At 18:17 the public-shelf scan lists RX-4816 as “not found”.
c002.f06b: At 18:17 the same scan lists RX-4814 and RX-4815 as present on the public shelf.
c002.f06c: The scan checks the public shelf only; it doesn't say where a missing parcel went or who moved it.
c002.e07.title: Parcel room access policy and floor plan
c002.e07.body:
Ground floor plan and staff access policy.

The back parcel room has one entrance, behind reception, and no other door or window. Only the concierge on reception duty is issued its key; cleaners use a separate supply closet and don't hold that key. The door is self-latching and the key isn't shared or left at the counter. The building manager confirms no spare key was issued and no emergency opening happened between 18:00 and 19:00.

There is no individual access log for the door, and no camera views the counter or the parcel room.
c002.f07a: Only the concierge on reception duty can enter the back parcel room; cleaners and residents can't.
c002.f07b: The back parcel room has one self-latching entrance behind reception, and no camera or individual access log.
c002.f07c: No spare key was issued and no emergency opening was recorded between 18:00 and 19:00.
c002.e08.title: Café receipt
c002.e08.body: Found on the reception counter. A receipt from the ground-floor café for two coffees, bought at 18:09. It names no buyer and mentions no parcel.
c002.f08a: A café receipt records two coffees bought at 18:09; it names no buyer and mentions no parcel.
c002.e09.title: Back parcel room inspection
c002.e09.body:
19:38. With the building manager's permission, the back parcel room is inspected.

In quarantine tray Q — a grey plastic bin on a metal shelf — is an unopened parcel labelled RX-4816 for Leah Moreno, flat 4B. The identifier matches the handover receipt and the seal is intact. An unsigned sticky note on the tray reads “Shelf wet — moved to Q”.

Neither the note nor the parcel shows who moved it.
c002.f09a: At 19:38 an unopened parcel labelled RX-4816 for Leah Moreno, flat 4B, was found in quarantine tray Q in the back parcel room.
c002.f09b: An unsigned sticky note on tray Q says: “Shelf wet — moved to Q”.
c002.f09c: The seal on RX-4816 was intact when it was found.
c002.e10.title: Reception staff rota
c002.e10.body:
Signed duty rota for 22 October 2026, confirmed by the building manager's staffing record.

18:00–19:00 — Mara Voss: reception (sole concierge)
18:00–19:00 — Nico Bell: cleaning (no back-room access)

No relief, handover or substitute was recorded in this hour.
c002.f10a: Mara Voss was the only concierge on reception duty from 18:00 to 19:00; no relief or substitute was assigned.
c002.f10b: Nico Bell was assigned cleaning duties, not reception or back-room access.
c002.d01.title: RX-4816 reached reception
c002.d01.description: Owen's account and the handover receipt describe the same 18:12 handover of the same uniquely numbered parcel. It arrived at Riverside reception.
c002.d02.title: Mara's account doesn't match the shelf scan
c002.d02.description: Mara says every parcel went onto the public shelf, yet at 18:17 the scan couldn't find RX-4816 there. Something happened to it between the handover and the scan.
c002.d03.title: The leak gave a reason to move a parcel
c002.d03.description: Water was dripping beside the public shelf at 18:16, and a minute later RX-4816 wasn't on it. A protective move is plausible, but where it went is still unknown.
c002.d04.title: Only Mara could use the back room
c002.d04.description: Only the duty concierge can enter the back parcel room, and Mara was the only concierge on duty from 18:00 to 19:00. If the parcel went into the back room, she had the only authorized access.
c002.d05.title: The missing parcel was in the back room
c002.d05.description: The parcel found in quarantine tray Q is the same RX-4816 that was handed to reception at 18:12.
c002.d06.title: It was moved to protect it, not stolen
c002.d06.description: The note on tray Q matches the leak reported at 18:16, and the parcel was unopened. Together with the back-room access, the best-supported explanation is that Mara moved it out of the wet for safekeeping.
c002.d07.title: “Delivered” didn't mean collected
c002.d07.description: The courier's status only records the handover at reception. It never said Leah had the parcel.
c002.d08.title: Nico couldn't reach the back room
c002.d08.description: Nico was near the leak, but cleaners have no back-room access and he was on cleaning duty. Being by the shelf doesn't give him a way into the parcel room.
c002.a01.title: Request permission to inspect the back parcel room
c002.a01.justification: RX-4816 reached reception but was gone from the public shelf minutes later. A leak could explain a protective move, and only the duty concierge could use the back room next to it. Ask the building manager for permission to look inside.
c002.c01.question: Who most likely last handled RX-4816 after reception accepted it?
c002.c02.question: What best explains the parcel's disappearance?
c002.c02.quarantine: It was moved to the back-room quarantine tray
c002.c02.resident_theft: A resident took it from the public shelf
c002.c02.courier_error: It was never handed over at Riverside
c002.hint.r01: Owen says he handed the parcel over. Does any document describe the same moment?
c002.hint.r02: Mara says every parcel went onto the public shelf. Did anything check the shelf afterwards?
c002.hint.r03: Something happened by the shelf just before the scan. Who reported it?
c002.hint.r04: Who could actually get into the back parcel room, and who was on duty that hour?
c002.hint.r05: Is the parcel in tray Q the one that was handed over at 18:12?
c002.hint.r06: The note on tray Q gives a reason. Does any earlier report match it?
c002.resolution:
Mara Voss moved the parcel to keep it dry.

Owen handed RX-4816 to reception at 18:12, and the receipt shows the same handover. The “delivered” notification only meant it had reached reception. At 18:16 Nico reported water dripping by the public shelf, and at 18:17 the shelf scan couldn't find RX-4816 there. Only the duty concierge can enter the back parcel room, and Mara was the only concierge on duty. That justified looking inside, where the unopened parcel sat in quarantine tray Q with a note: “Shelf wet — moved to Q”.

What remains uncertain: nobody saw Mara move the parcel, and the note is unsigned. The reconstruction rests on exclusive access, the rota and the recovery together. A borrowed key or an undocumented exception can't be ruled out entirely, which is why the question asks who most likely handled it.

Afterwards, Mara explained that she moved the parcel out of the drip and forgot to tell Leah. That closes the story, but it was never part of the proof. Leah got her lens that evening.
